easy.def: Having to do with school.
examples: An academic subject.
Academic work is hard.
Her academic grades are good.

more.def: Having to do with school and learning.
examples: Math is an academic subject.
The academic year starts in September.
He gets academic help after school.

easy.def: A special school.
examples: She goes to a music academy.
The academy trains dancers.
The academy is by the river.

more.def: A school that teaches a special subject or skill.
examples: She goes to a music academy on weekends.
The soccer academy trains young players.
He studied at the art academy.

easy.def: A way of speaking that shows where you are from.
examples: She has a British accent.
He has a southern accent.
I love his accent.

more.def: A way of pronouncing words that shows which country or place you come from.
examples: She speaks with a British accent.
His accent told us he was from the south.
I tried to copy my cousin's accent.

easy.def: To take something that is given to you.
examples: I accept the gift.
She accepted the prize.
He accepts the cookie.

more.def: To take something that is offered to you.
examples: She accepted the prize with a smile.
Will you accept my invitation to the party?
The cashier accepts coins and bills.

easy.def: Good enough.
examples: The grade is acceptable.
The plan is acceptable.
Is this acceptable?

more.def: Good enough to be allowed or approved.
examples: The grade was acceptable.
Quiet talk is acceptable in the hall.
The plan was acceptable to everyone.

easy.def: Agreeing to take something or let it be.
examples: She smiled in acceptance.
The acceptance of the gift made him glad.
Acceptance helped her feel at home.

more.def: The act of agreeing to take something, or of welcoming a person or idea as part of a group.
examples: His acceptance of the invitation made the whole family glad.
The new girl was glad to feel the acceptance of her classmates.
Tom learned acceptance when his team lost the game and he shook hands anyway.

easy.def: The way to get in or use something.
examples: We have access to the library.
There is access to the beach.
Do you have access?

more.def: The ability or right to enter, use or get something.
examples: The students have access to the library.
A path gives access to the beach.
Everyone has access to clean water.

easy.def: Something bad that happens that no one wanted to happen.
examples: I spilled my milk by accident.
There was a car accident on our street.
Dropping the plate was an accident.

more.def: Something that happens by chance and is not planned, often causing harm or damage.
examples: He broke the vase by accident when he bumped the table.
We met by accident at the grocery store.
Wearing a helmet can protect you in a bike accident.

easy.def: Not done on purpose.
examples: It was an accidental spill.
The bump was accidental.
The mistake was accidental.

more.def: Happening by chance, not planned or done on purpose.
examples: The spill was accidental, so nobody was upset.
Their meeting at the park was accidental, but they became good friends.
The accidental discovery of the old coin surprised the class.

easy.def: By mistake.
examples: I accidentally dropped it.
She accidentally broke the cup.
He accidentally sat on my hat.

more.def: In a way that was not planned, by mistake.
examples: I accidentally dropped my book in the puddle.
She accidentally knocked over the milk.
The baker accidentally used salt instead of sugar.

easy.def: To have enough room for someone or something.
examples: The hall can accommodate fifty people.
Our car accommodates five.
The tent accommodates two.

more.def: To have enough room for people or things, or to give someone what they need.
examples: The hotel can accommodate two hundred guests.
The school changed the schedule to accommodate the sports teams.
Our van accommodates the whole band and all their instruments.

easy.def: To go with someone.
examples: I accompany Mom to the store.
The dog accompanies us.
She accompanied her friend.

more.def: To go with someone to a place, or to play music while someone sings.
examples: I accompanied Mom to the store.
The dog accompanied us on our walk.
She accompanied the singer on the piano.

easy.def: To finish something you set out to do.
examples: We accomplished our goal.
She accomplished a lot today.
He accomplished the task.

more.def: To succeed in doing something, especially something that took effort.
examples: We accomplished our goal of cleaning the park.
She accomplished a lot by working hard.
He accomplished the long climb before sunset.

easy.def: Something good that you finish.
examples: Finishing the race was an accomplishment.
The accomplishment was big.
She is proud of her accomplishment.

more.def: Something you have done well, especially after trying hard.
examples: Finishing the race was a real accomplishment.
She is proud of her accomplishment in learning to swim.
Climbing the tall tree was a great accomplishment.

easy.def: As said by.
examples: According to Mom, it is time for bed.
According to the map, we turn here.
According to the weather report, it will rain.

more.def: As said by someone or shown by something.
examples: According to the map, we turn left here.
According to my teacher, the test is Friday.
The park is closed, according to the sign.

easy.def: A story that tells what happened.
examples: She gave an account of the trip.
The account was short.
He wrote an account of the storm.

more.def: A report or story that tells what happened.
examples: She gave an account of the trip to her class.
He wrote an account of the storm for the newspaper.
The explorer's account was published.

easy.def: Money kept in a bank.
examples: I have an account at the bank.
Mom put money in my account.
The account has ten dollars.

more.def: An arrangement with a bank where your money is kept safe.
examples: She opened a savings account with her birthday money.
Dad checks his account online.
I put five dollars in my account.

easy.def: A person who keeps track of money.
examples: The accountant counts money.
My uncle is an accountant.
The accountant works with numbers.

more.def: A person whose job is to keep and check records of money for people or businesses.
examples: My uncle is an accountant who works with numbers.
The accountant checked the figures.
The accountant helped the company plan.

easy.def: Correct.
examples: The map is accurate.
Her answer is accurate.
The clock is accurate.

more.def: Free from mistakes, exactly right.
examples: The map is accurate and shows every road.
Her answer was accurate and complete.
The clock is accurate to the second.

easy.def: Saying that someone did something wrong.
examples: The accusation was false.
He made an accusation.
She denied the accusation.

more.def: A statement that someone has done something wrong.
examples: The accusation was not true.
He denied the accusation.
The teacher looked into the accusation.

easy.def: To say someone did something wrong.
examples: Do not accuse me.
He accused his brother of taking it.
They accused the cat.

more.def: To say that someone has done something wrong, especially without being sure.
examples: She accused her friend of eating the last cookie.
It is wrong to accuse someone without proof.
The farmer accused the fox of stealing the hens.

easy.def: Used to something.
examples: I am accustomed to the cold.
She is accustomed to early mornings.
We got accustomed to it.

more.def: Used to something, so that it feels normal.
examples: I am accustomed to the cold winters.
She is accustomed to getting up early.
The puppy grew accustomed to its new home.

easy.def: A card with one spot.
examples: I got an ace.
The ace is high.
An ace is a card.

more.def: A playing card with a single spot, which is often the highest card.
examples: I drew an ace of hearts.
The ace beat the king.
The deck has four aces.

easy.def: A person who is very good at something.
examples: She is an ace at chess.
He is an ace pilot.
The team's ace pitched well.

more.def: Someone who is very skilled at something.
examples: She is an ace at math.
The team's ace pitcher struck out the batter.
He is an ace on his bike.

easy.def: To have a steady pain.
examples: My tooth aches.
My legs ache after the run.
His back ached.

more.def: To hurt with a dull pain that does not go away quickly.
examples: My legs ache after the long hike.
His tooth ached all night.
Her tired feet ached after a day of walking.

easy.def: A pain that lasts for a while but is not sharp.
examples: I have an ache in my tummy.
Her arm has an ache.
The ache went away.

more.def: A steady pain that continues for a time.
examples: He had an ache in his back after lifting the box.
A dull ache in my tooth kept me awake.
The ache in her legs went away after she rested.

easy.def: To do something you worked hard for.
examples: You can achieve your goal if you keep trying.
He achieved his goal of riding a bike.
I want to achieve a high score.

more.def: To succeed in doing something through effort or skill.
examples: She achieved her dream of swimming across the lake.
The class achieved its goal of reading one hundred books.
You can achieve a lot when you practice every day.

easy.def: Something good that you worked hard to do.
examples: Reading a whole book was an achievement.
Winning the race was her achievement.
He is proud of his achievement.

more.def: Something important that a person has done well, usually after hard work.
examples: Finishing the whole marathon was a big achievement for her.
The class was proud of its achievement in raising money for the shelter.
Landing on the moon was one of the great achievements in history.

easy.def: A sour liquid that can eat away at things.
examples: Lemon juice has acid.
The acid is sour.
Acid can burn.

more.def: A kind of substance that tastes sour and can burn or wear things away.
examples: Lemon juice contains a weak acid.
Strong acid can burn your skin.
Scientists test whether a liquid is an acid.

easy.def: To say that something is true.
examples: I acknowledge my mistake.
She acknowledged the gift.
He acknowledged the problem.

more.def: To admit that something is true, or to show that you have noticed something.
examples: I acknowledge that I made a mistake.
She acknowledged the gift with a thank-you note.
He waved to acknowledge the crowd.

easy.def: A person you know a little.
examples: She is an acquaintance.
He met an old acquaintance.
We are acquaintances.

more.def: A person you know a little, but who is not a close friend.
examples: She is an acquaintance from my class.
He met an old acquaintance at the store.
We are acquaintances, not close friends.

easy.def: To get something.
examples: I acquire new skills.
She acquired a new pet.
We acquired a book.

more.def: To get or gain something, usually by effort.
examples: I acquired a new skill by practicing.
The museum acquired an old painting.
She acquired a taste for spicy food.

easy.def: A measure of land.
examples: The farm has ten acres.
An acre is big.
We own an acre.

more.def: A unit for measuring land, a bit smaller than a football field.
examples: The farm has ten acres of corn.
An acre is about the size of a football field.
We own half an acre of land.

easy.def: From one side to the other.
examples: Walk across the street.
A bridge goes across the river.
We swam across the lake.

more.def: From one side of something to the other.
examples: A bridge stretches across the river.
She ran across the field.
He drew a line across the page.

easy.def: From one side to the other.
examples: The lake is a mile across.
The kids ran across and waved.
We got across by boat.

more.def: To or on the other side.
examples: The lake is a mile across at its widest point.
The kids ran across and waved from the far side.
The river is wide, but we can get across by boat.

easy.def: To play a part in a play.
examples: I act in the school play.
She acted like a dragon.
We act out the story.

more.def: To play a character in a play, movie or show.
examples: She will act the part of a queen in the school play.
Many actors begin to act when they are very young.
The twins acted out a funny scene for the class.

easy.def: To behave in a certain way.
examples: My baby brother acts shy.
The dog acts scared in a storm.
Try to act calm.

more.def: To behave in a particular way.
examples: My little brother acts shy around strangers.
The puppy acted scared when it heard the thunder.
Try to act calmly if a bee flies near you.

easy.def: Something that someone does.
examples: Sharing your snack is a kind act.
Saving the cat was a brave act.
Cleaning the park was a good act.

more.def: A single thing that a person does.
examples: Picking up litter at the beach was a simple act that helped the birds.
The firefighter's brave act saved the little dog.
An act of kindness can make someone's whole day better.

easy.def: Something you do.
examples: Cleaning up was a kind action.
His quick action helped.
She took action and called for help.

more.def: Something that you do.
examples: Her kind action made me smile.
A quick action saved the toy from falling.
He took action and called for help.

easy.def: To turn on or start something.
examples: I activate the alarm.
Press this to activate the machine.
Dad activated the light.

more.def: To make something start working.
examples: I pressed the button to activate the alarm.
The motion of the door activates the light.
She activated the phone using a code.

easy.def: Moving around a lot.
examples: The puppy is active.
I stay active.
She leads an active life.

more.def: Full of energy and busy doing things.
examples: The puppy is very active and loves to run.
He stays active by riding his bike every day.
Active children need lots of sleep.

easy.def: Something you do for fun or to learn.
examples: Our class did an art activity.
Swimming is my favorite activity.
The camp has many activities.

more.def: Something that people do, usually for fun or interest.
examples: Painting is my favorite activity.
The camp has many activities, such as swimming and hiking.
The class did an activity to learn about the stars.

easy.def: A person who plays a part in a play or movie.
examples: The actor played a king.
My uncle is an actor.
The actors bowed.

more.def: A person who plays a character in a play, movie or show.
examples: The actor played the part of a pirate.
My aunt is a famous actor.
The actors bowed to the cheering crowd.

easy.def: A woman who acts in plays or movies.
examples: The actress played a queen.
She is an actress.
The actress was on stage.

more.def: A woman who acts in plays, movies or TV shows.
examples: The actress played a queen in the school play.
My aunt is an actress.
The actress took a bow.

easy.def: Real and true.
examples: The actual price was low.
This is the actual story.
The actual size is small.

more.def: Real, not made up, and really so.
examples: The actual price was less than I thought.
The movie is based on an actual event.
What is the actual size of the fish?

easy.def: In fact, or really.
examples: I am actually seven.
It actually works.
She actually won.

more.def: Used to say what is true, especially when it is surprising.
examples: The tomato is actually a fruit, not a vegetable.
I thought the test would be hard, but it was actually easy.
He actually caught the ball with one hand.
